Dear Ms. Sandoval:

         In accordance with 17.9.530.9 NMAC, Southwestern Public Service Company (“SPS”)
submits to the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (“Commission”) its Application for:
(1) Revision of Its Retail Rates Under Advice Notice No. 341; And (2) Other Associated Relief
(“Application”) and proposed form of Notice; Advice Notice No. 341 and proposed Rate
Schedules; Direct Testimony and Attachments; and a Certificate of Service. Included with this
filing is Hardy McLean’s check in the amount of $45.00 in payment of the Commission’s fee for
filing its application and SPS’s new or changed Rates, Rules and Forms in accordance with
17.1.210.12(D) NMAC.

        The proposed rates in Advice Notice No. 341 will become effective on December 20, 2025
unless the Commission suspends the proposed rates by that date in accordance with Sections 62-
8-7(B) and (C) of the Public Utility Act (“PUA”). 1

        SPS’s current rates for New Mexico retail electric service were approved and authorized
by the Commission in the Final Order Adopting Certification of Stipulation in Case No. 22-00286-
UT, issued on October 19, 2023. Those rates are no longer just and reasonable and do not allow
SPS to recover a reasonable return on its investment in its public utility plant and property to serve
SPS’s New Mexico retail customers. Further, SPS’s rates and revenues, as currently allocated, do
not reflect SPS’s cost of service for its separate classes of retail electric customers. Three broad
areas are driving the need for changes in rates: (1) significant grid investments needed to support
the evolving and increasing needs of customers, as well as Xcel Energy Inc. (“Xcel Energy”) and
New Mexico’s clean energy goals; (2) investment in a changing generation portfolio as SPS is
retiring aging units, extending the lives of select plants, and investing in new sources of generation;
and (3) the mix of SPS’s wholesale and retail customers, and the balance between its New Mexico

        SPS’s rate case filing uses a base period of July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025 (“Base
Period”); an adjusted base period of July 1, 2024 through June 30, 2025 (“Adjusted Base Period”);
a linkage data timeframe of July 1, 2025 and November 30, 2026 (“Linkage Data”); and a future
test year of December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2027 (“Future Test Year”). SPS also
requests to include in rate base the new capital investment SPS placed in service during the Base
Period and the capital investment SPS forecasts it will place in service through November 30,
2027.
        SPS’s proposed Test Year revenue requirement is $892,652,373. This revenue requirement
reflects an increase of $175,354,544 in base revenue over current non-fuel base revenue, which is
a 24.25% increase in base rate revenues and an approximate 16.73% in total revenue, for the Future
Test Year.

                  SOUTHWESTERN PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY’S
            APPLICATION FOR AUTHORITY TO CHANGE RATES AND FOR
                   OTHER APPROVALS AND AUTHORIZATIONS

I.     Statement of Requested Relief

       1.      Southwestern Public Service Company (“SPS”) requests authority to change its

base rates and certain other approvals, as detailed below. Through this filing, SPS seeks to continue

to provide reliable and cost-effective energy to the growing communities of Southeastern New

Mexico. SPS is at an important juncture in its generation and infrastructure planning. It is

transitioning its generation fleet by retiring and replacing aging units and extending the operating

lives of select cost-effective plants. As part of that transition, SPS seeks recovery of recently

approved investment in new solar and battery projects. At the same time, SPS is making necessary

investments in its information technology, transmission, and distribution infrastructure to support

sustained load-growth and to harden the system against increasing security threats, extreme
 weather, and wildfire risk. SPS is also seeking recovery of previously deferred costs, like increases

in excess liability insurance premiums, technology upgrades, and meter replacement costs—costs

that reflect a changing energy landscape. Additionally, SPS is updating its capital structure to

reflect current financial conditions and help maintain a strong credit profile so that it can continue

to provide reliable power to New Mexico’s growing economy. Finally, New Mexico’s increasing

share of SPS’s retail load is driving jurisdictional and customer-class allocation changes. As a

result of these changes, SPS’s current base rates, which were approved in Case No. 22-00286-UT,

are no longer just and reasonable.

       2.      SPS’s rate filing follows the framework established by NMSA 1978, §§ 62-8-7, 62-

3-3(P), and 62-6-14(D) of the Public Utility Act, and 17.1.3 NMAC (the “Future Test Year Rule”)

and 17.9.530 NMAC (“Rule 530”). Thus, the filing includes cost of service data from three time

periods: the Base and Adjusted Base Periods, the Linkage Data Timeframe, and the Future Test

Year, defined as follows:

                   •   Base and Adjusted Base Period. The Base Period covers July 1, 2024
                       through June 30, 2025. It reflects SPS’s unadjusted accounting data as
                       recorded on the SPS’s books in accordance with the Future Test Year Rule.
                       The Adjusted Base Period covers the same timeframe, but includes
                       adjustments such as unblended plant depreciation rates, accounting
                       annualizations and normalizations, and weather-normalized revenues.

                   •   Linkage Data Timeframe. The Linkage Data Timeframe spans July 1, 2025
                       through November 30, 2026. The Linkage Data Timeframe is not a test
                       period but provides Linkage Data establishing a “verifiable link” between
                       the Base/Adjusted Base Period and the Future Test Year based on known
                       and measurable cost adjustments.

                   •   Future Test Year. The Future Test Year runs from December 1, 2026
                       through November 30, 2027. It includes capital additions that entered
                       service after July 1, 2024 and those expected to be placed in service through
                       November 30, 2027, along with Base-Period expenses adjusted for known
                       and measurable changes, such as increases in labor, compensation, and
                       benefits.

                                                  2

                56% equity ratio, an authorized return on equity (“ROE”) of 10.5%, and a cost of

VII.   Summary of Proposed Rate Changes


                                                  9
        18.     SPS’s current rates for New Mexico retail electric service, which were approved

and authorized by the Commission in Case No. 22-00286-UT, are no longer just and reasonable

and do not allow SPS to recover a reasonable return on its investment in its public utility plant and

property that serve SPS’s New Mexico retail customers. Further, SPS’s rates, authorized revenues,

and cost allocations do not adequately reflect SPS’s cost of service for its separate classes of New

Mexico retail electric customers. These matters are fully discussed and supported in SPS’s

pre-filed direct testimony and rate filing package. SPS’s proposed rates for the Future Test Year

will allow SPS to recover its revenue requirement and, therefore, the proposed rates are just and

reasonable and should be approved by the Commission.

       19.     In this rate case, SPS uses a Base Period and Adjusted Base Period of July 1, 2024

through June 30, 2025, and a Future Test Year of December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2027.

SPS developed its Future Test Year data by starting with the Base Period data, adjusting that data

through normalizations and annualizations to produce an Adjusted Base Period, and then providing

linkage data to show how the Adjusted Base Period data was adjusted to produce the Future Test

Year revenue requirement. Specifically, to develop its Future Test Year data, SPS has: (1) utilized

its Capital Budget for the Base Period, Linkage Data Timeframe and Future Test Year; (2) applied

known and measurable adjustments to its Adjusted Base Period non-labor O&M expenses; and (3)

escalated its Adjusted Base Period labor-related O&M expenses (compensation and benefits)

based on increases that are expected to occur between the end of the Base Period and the Future

Test Year. In their direct testimony, Ms. Johnson, Ms. Newman, and Mr. Schrubbe explain the

development of this Future Test Year data in detail.



                                                 10
        20.     As explained in this filing, SPS has made and plans on making significant capital

investment to benefit its customers and maintain continued reliability of electric service, which

creates a need for additional revenues for SPS’s New Mexico retail services. This investment

amounts to a total of $1,794,651,600 on a New Mexico retail basis.

       21.     In addition, since SPS’s last base rate case, jurisdictional allocations have changed

among SPS’s New Mexico retail, Texas retail, and wholesale customers due to retail load growth

in SPS’s New Mexico service area and declining wholesale sales.

VIII. Technical Conferences and Rerunning Supporting Programs

       22.     In accordance with the Future Test Year Rule and Rule 530, SPS proposes to hold

a series of technical conferences to answer questions Staff and Intervenors may have about SPS’s

jurisdictional cost of service model, its class cost of service study model, and other models and

software SPS has relied upon for this case. In addition, for programs that are not downloadable to

fully functional and executable spreadsheets, SPS will rerun such supporting programs for input

changes reasonably required by Staff or Intervenors to enable these parties to capture the effect of

such proposed input changes on the Future Test Year jurisdictional cost of service model, as

required by 17.1.3.11(B) NMAC.

IX.    Settlement Conferences

Commission establish a procedural schedule that includes conducting a settlement conference(s).

package schedules, workpapers, transmittal letter, and other documentation, SPS respectfully

              (1)      grant the relief described and discussed in Section I of this Application;

              (2)      suspend the proposed rates and set a public hearing concerning the justness
